mocks.intro: Practise here for free, then book a live mock with a real interviewer when you want pressure.

types.label: Coding
types.hint: Talk out loud. Start with an example, then brute force, then improve. Handle edge cases last.

questions.title: Clean a messy client CSV
questions.prompt: A hospital sends a 50,000-row CSV of patients. Names are dirty, dates mix DD/MM and MM/DD, and 8% of rows are duplicates. Write a function that returns a clean table and a one-page summary of what you fixed. What would you ask the client before you start?

questions.title: Merge two client systems
questions.prompt: Client A has users in Postgres (email as key). Client B has users in a REST API (phone as key). Some people exist in both. Design and sketch code to produce a single customer list without losing anyone. How do you handle conflicts?

questions.title: SQL: top failing workflows
questions.prompt: Tables: events(id, client_id, workflow, status, latency_ms, ts). Write SQL for: the 5 workflows with the worst p95 latency in the last 7 days, per client, ignoring test accounts. Then explain how you would index this.

questions.title: Rate-limit an LLM endpoint
questions.prompt: Your RAG chatbot is blowing the OpenAI budget. Implement a per-tenant rate limiter and a fallback when the model is down. What metrics do you log?

types.label: Behavioral
types.hint: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. End with what you learned. Keep it under two minutes.

questions.title: Impossible deadline
questions.prompt: The client is aggressive and the deadline is impossible. What do you do this week, and what do you say in the room?

questions.title: Unclear requirements
questions.prompt: You join a project and nobody can explain what 'done' means. Walk through your first 72 hours.

questions.title: You were wrong
questions.prompt: Tell me about a time your technical recommendation was wrong in front of a customer. What did you do next?

questions.title: Why FDE / AI Engineer?
questions.prompt: Why this role, why now, and why not a core product SWE job? Give a specific story, not a generic answer.

types.label: Case study
types.hint: Restate the problem, list assumptions, pick a thin slice, show trade-offs (time vs accuracy vs cost).

questions.title: Hospital document chaos
questions.prompt: A hospital has 12 years of PDFs, scans and emails. They want 'an AI that answers clinician questions with sources'. Scope a 6-week pilot. What do you build first, what data do you need, and how do you measure success?

questions.title: Fraud alerts that nobody trusts
questions.prompt: A fintech client's fraud model flags 4,000 cases a day. Analysts look at 200. Design a workflow (human + AI) that triples useful reviews without missing high-risk cases.

questions.title: Sales wants a demo tomorrow
questions.prompt: A VP promised a live demo of 'our AI copilot' in 24 hours on the client's own data. The data is a 2GB Excel dump you have not seen. Plan the day. What do you refuse to fake?

types.label: System design
types.hint: Start with users and scale. Draw the path of one request. Call out failure modes and cost.

questions.title: Multi-tenant RAG
questions.prompt: Design a RAG service used by 40 enterprise clients. Each client has private documents. Cover ingest, retrieval, tenancy, evals, and what happens when one client uploads malware.

questions.title: Client data pipeline
questions.prompt: Design a pipeline that pulls from Salesforce, a warehouse, and three CSVs every night, then serves a dashboard by 8am. Talk consistency, retries, and alerting.

book.title: Free self-practice
book.note: Use the timer on this page. Record yourself. Score honestly.

book.title: Peer mock (Pramp)
book.note: Swap 45-minute interviews with another candidate. Good for coding rust.

book.title: Structured mocks (Exponent)
book.note: Coaches for product, engineering and case-style rounds. Useful for FDE presentations.

book.title: Anonymous live mock (interviewing.io)
book.note: Real interviewers from top companies. Closest thing to the real loop.

jobs.intro: Apply in public, then ask for a referral. A warm intro beats a cold apply almost every time.

linkedin.intro: Connect with people who already do the job. Ask for 15 minutes, not a referral in the first message.

peopleSearches.label: Posts: FDE day in the life

templates.title: Connection request (no ask yet)
templates.text: Hi {name} — I am preparing for Forward Deployed / AI Engineer roles and have been following your work at {company}. Would be glad to connect and learn from people actually doing the job.

templates.title: After they accept: 15-minute chat
templates.text: Thanks for connecting, {name}. I am {your background in one line}. I am targeting FDE / applied AI roles in the next few months and would value 15 minutes on what the loop actually tests. Happy to send a short agenda. No pressure if timing is bad.

templates.title: Referral ask (only after a chat)
templates.text: Thanks again for the time last week, {name}. I applied to {role} at {company} (link: {url}). If you are open to a referral I can send a 5-line summary + resume. If not, I appreciate the advice either way.
